summary: Two range lights on the Lake Superior mainland near Christmas, Michigan, first lit in 1868 to guide ships into Grand Island harbor; the front light is on the 2025 Light List.

structures.note: Present front-light tower; replaced the earlier front light in 1983. The 1868 front tower was a wooden tower, replaced by a white mast in 1920 (LighthouseFriends)

Conical steel tower erected about 125 yards behind the keeper's dwelling in 1913 (LighthouseFriends). USLHS gives the tower as 62 ft (18.9 m) and the focal height as 70 ft above mean high water. Rear light discontinued 1969.
Seven-room dwelling with a rectangular tower on one gable end, built for the rear light; sold and moved to Munising (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Beside M-28 near Christmas. Towers owned by the Forest Service and managed by Hiawatha National Forest. LighthouseFriends: grounds open, towers closed. Munising Visitor's Bureau: periodic free tours of the rear light in summer, subject to staffing. USLHS: Open to Public: Yes. Do not climb the towers.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Munising visitor guide and some listings say the range was built in 1867; LighthouseFriends and the record put the first light in 1868 (first lit 15 August 1868). The story uses 1868.

The 2025 Light List lists Bay Furnace Light (LLNR 14600) as a working light, and USLHS lists the range as an active aid to navigation. The undated Munising guide says both lights are inactive. The story reports both and does not settle it.

LighthouseFriends says grounds open and towers closed; the Munising guide says the Forest Service runs periodic free tours of the rear light in summer; USLHS says Open to Public: Yes. The story points readers to the Ranger District and says not to climb.

LighthouseFriends says Kuhn served nineteen years at the range lights and died in 1895; the roster's dates (1876 to 1894) give eighteen years and end his stint in 1894. The story gives the roster dates, states LighthouseFriends' nineteen years, and does not reconcile them.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination for NRIS 90000906 is not digitised (the NPGallery PDF is a 22 KB placeholder), so the story rests mainly on LighthouseFriends, which is copyrighted and used for facts only (paraphrased, with short quotations). Only one short primary source is cited for the 1860s; the Lighthouse Board corpus begins in 1891, and no 1860s or 1868 report or Michigan newspaper hit was found (searches of Chronicling America for 1867-1869 returned nothing). The 1891 winch entry is read from OCR (scan 204); printed page unconfirmed; check the image. The 1913 Bulletin change (oil to acetylene) is read from OCR; the Bulletin index lists the item at p. 81. The roster line 'Casper Kuhn (1876-1894)' conflicts with LighthouseFriends' 1895 death date. Beedon's later service at Au Sable is not dated in the sources read, so no other_stations entry is made for him. The record's 'Sources differ on whether the light is still lit' is answered only partly: the Light List (2025) shows a working front light; the Munising guide says inactive. Facts: the record's focal height 6.1 m and characteristic match the Light List; the Light List range is 6 nm, the record 5.2 nm. Structures: USLHS gives the rear tower as 70 ft above mean high water, steel, conical, established 1913; the record's 20 m figure and 1868 date are not supported. The front light's 1868 tower is gone (1920 mast, 1983 cylindrical tower). Do not visit or climb closed towers; access is for the Ranger District to confirm. Wrecks: none tied to the range in the sources read. The Munising guide's 'Established 1867' is an undated tourism page and is not used as the year of first light. Second pass: the 1913 Bulletin entry for this range is on PDF p. 33 (corpus grep and the page text), not the printed p. 81 the earlier draft gave; the source now cites p. 33. The Munising guide's 'Established in 1867' is quoted as the guide's claim and is not used for the first-light year. The 1868 first light is LighthouseFriends' date (15 August 1868). The keeper roster is USLHS (from NARA registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory), matched by name and position; the roster lists six principal keepers and no assistants. Kuhn's nineteen years (LighthouseFriends) conflict with the roster's 1876-1894 dates; both are stated. Beedon's Au Sable service is named by LighthouseFriends but not dated, so no other_stations entry is made for him. The NPGallery pages give 'Date Published' (record date) for NRIS 90000906; the story does not call it a listing date. Fact-check 2026-10-22 (second reader): the opening no longer says the lights guide ships as a present fact, because the 2025 Light List (front light active) and the undated Munising guide (both inactive) disagree on status; the story says the lights were built to guide ships. The 1863 committee words are cited as LighthouseFriends quotes them. The 1913 Bulletin link uses the _0.pdf file that corpus.py cite prints; the entry is at PDF p. 33. The 1915 Commissioner entry is in the list of aids in commission on 30 June 1915 under the acetylene heading (printed p. 37, scan p. 42), so 'still shows' is dated to that list. The 'do not climb' advice is attributed to LighthouseFriends (towers closed), not to the Munising guide, which does not say it. The 1891 winch entry sits under the 1891 running head and the Eleventh District heading (scan p. 204; printed page not confirmed). The Light List row (LLNR 14600) matches the story. Units: 125 yards (114 m), 375 feet (114 m) and 20 feet (6 m) are added. The 1913 Bulletin's section heading is not quoted because it was not confirmed on the page.
